gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold entry bundles two independently diagnosable defects in the same block-shift theorem and its application. ISSUE-001 directly identifies the incorrect coefficient condition and reciprocal eigenvalue/pole cancellation mismatch, while ISSUE-002 independently identifies the failure of the stated invertibility-based application for singular Lambda_{R,1} cases. Together they recognize the full failure of the theorem's polynomiality/spectral claims and its claimed application domain.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The stated left-shift hypothesis is mismatched with the displayed rational factor: it imposes cancellation at reciprocal locations rather than at the poles of the factor, so polynomiality and the associated shifted-spectrum claim do not follow. Independently, requiring invertible S_1=S^{-1} when Lambda_{R,1} may be singular excludes permitted infinite-eigenvalue cases and leaves the application and downstream transformed-QME premise unjustified.
gold_decisions.combination_explanation: The gold issue contains two distinct substantive defects: (1) an algebraic/pole-cancellation and spectral-orientation error in the theorem statement, and (2) a separate domain/invertibility failure in applying the theorem to singular Lambda_{R,1} cases. ISSUE-001 independently diagnoses the first through the corrected coefficient condition, determinant/eigenvalue interpretation, and repair. ISSUE-002 independently diagnoses the second through the zero eigenvalue caused by an infinite lambda, the resulting nonexistent invertible S_1, and an inverse-free singular-compatible repair. No additional mathematical connection is supplied by the combination.

component_coverage.gold_component: Incorrect hypothesis and reciprocal pole/eigenvalue assignment fail to establish polynomiality and the shifted-spectrum claim.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 gives the corrected coefficient ordering required by the displayed transformation, explains that the poles are associated with eigenvalues of S_1 rather than S_1^{-1}, states the resulting inconsistency, and supplies a theorem repair.

component_coverage.gold_component: The theorem's invertibility requirement prevents its application to permitted singular Lambda_{R,1} cases, including Example 1, so downstream transformed-QME and reduced-system claims are not uniformly established.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 explicitly identifies the required invertibility, the zero eigenvalue arising from an infinite lambda, the resulting inability to invoke the theorem, the unsupported factorization and downstream QME derivation, and an inverse-free repair allowing singular cases.
